analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the canonical index and selected boundary details. ProtocolCodec.swift:226–230 adds JSON-encoded busy reason, timestamp and optional add-on identifier to the raw-attestation registration path; existing attestation bytes, encryption capabilities, credentials and strict App Attest resume validation are unchanged. ProviderBusy.swift:30–47 introduces flat optional fields, treats unknown reasons as absent and defaults a missing timestamp to zero. This is provider-reported availability metadata, not verified trust evidence (TB-002, T-052, T-055); no supplied code uses it to grant authorization or billing credit. No concrete regression is established by these serializers.
Messages.swift:1710–2085 was examined; this excerpt lies outside its mapped changes and retains encrypted request envelopes, authorization diagnostics and control-message dispatch. It does not establish how the new busy fields are populated or how draining status is enforced.
ProviderLoop+AppAttestShadow.swift:115,120 changes both update-resumption guards from refusing to refusingForServiceChange while preserving shutdown, idle-update, generation and retirement checks. Integration must inspect that predicate and add-on hold lifecycle to confirm worker resumption can maintain attestation during a hold without permitting inference, bypassing update retirement or weakening connection invalidation (TB-011, T-053, T-057). Also reconcile register/heartbeat encoding and local request admission across reconnects: busy metadata alone does not demonstrate exclusion before the first heartbeat, and coordinator consumption is an external contract, not an observed missing control. These material cross-file questions remain unresolved in this source scope; no supported finding concerns plaintext exposure, privilege, model integrity or payment changes.
